text: Patterns of Instrumental and Informational Workplace Health Support Use Among Hospital Service Workers of Low- to Mid-Socioeconomic Status. PurposeTo examine workplace health supports (WHS) use and sociodemographic and organizational correlates among healthcare workers predominantly of low- to mid-socioeconomic status (SES).DesignCross-sectional survey.SettingLarge U.S. healthcare system, 2018.Sample1283 healthcare service workers; 1196 included in final analyses (93.2%).MeasuresInstrumental and informational WHS use; SES; race; age; shift; sex; obesity; organizational health climate; coworker support; supervisor support.AnalysisPearson point biserial correlations (rpb), phi (Φ) statistics, and multivariable negative binomial regression models were used. Interaction terms between organizational health climate and sociodemographic characteristics were tested.ResultsThe median employee used two WHS (one instrumental, one informational). Older age was associated with greater informational WHS use (Φ = .13 to .21), while Black race was associated with greater instrumental WHS use (Φ = .09 to .15). Organizational health climate was modestly associated with healthy eating and physical activity WHS (rpb = .09 to .11). In adjusted models, age, race, and organizational health climate remained independently associated with WHS use. Modest interaction effects were observed between organizational health climate and race (total and informational models) and sex (total model).ConclusionDifferentiating WHS by support type reveals meaningful differences in engagement across worker groups. Findings highlight the importance of organizational context. Results should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and self-reported measures.

Clinical Hypnosis as a Supportive Nonpharmacological Intervention for Distress and Pain in Older Adults in Hospital Settings: A Scoping Review. This scoping review mapped the available evidence on clinical hypnosis as an adjunctive intervention for older adults in hospital and geriatric care, focusing on anxiety, distress, depression, pain, and intervention delivery.

Minimal-Burden Prosthodontics: Simple Care and Comprehensive Risk Assessment in Older Adults. Older adults represent a growing population in whom oral health impairment may affect comfort, nutrition, dignity, social participation, and quality of life. Conventional prosthodontic approaches, often guided by comprehensive rehabilitation, technical refinement, and long-term restorative ideals, require assessment of present and foreseeable functional, cognitive, and maintenance needs.

Agreement Between In-Person and Telephone Application of the Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly. Remote cognitive assessment has gained prominence due to limited access to in-person services. The purpose was to investigate the agreement between in-person and telephone administration of the Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE).

Relationship between objective sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese: Results by work in the Shika study. Sleep quality and work, as factors related to psychological distress, have not yet been elucidated. Additionally, few studies have examined the association between sleep efficiency and psychological distress, which may affect psychological distress in middle-aged and older adults according to their work status. This study aimed to examine and clarify the relationship between sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese stratified by work and sex.
